Below is a step-by-step recipe for adding a **hillshade** layer that draws its relief from a **raster-DEM** source. Everything you need is in the style JSON (or the `addSource` / `addLayer` calls you make from JavaScript). --- ## 1. Choose / host a DEM source MapLibre GL JS can read any raster-DEM that follows the **Mapbox Terrain-RGB** encoding (or any other 16-bit elevation format that the library can decode). Typical public options: | Provider | URL template | Notes | |----------|--------------|-------| | **MapLibre demo tiles** | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Small world-wide DEM, good for demos | | **OpenMapTiles Terrain** | `https://tiles.openmaptiles.org/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Same format as Mapbox Terrain-RGB | | **Your own tiles** | `https://my.cdn.com/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Must be PNG (or JPEG) with Terrain-RGB encoding | > **Tip:** If you already have a GeoTIFF, you can convert it to Terrain-RGB tiles with tools like **gdal2tiles.py** (`-a 0,0,0` for elevation) or **tippecanoe** + **mapbox/terrain-rgb** scripts. --- ## 2. Add the raster-DEM source to the map ```js map.addSource('dem', { type: 'raster-dem', // <-- important: tells MapLibre this is a DEM url: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', tileSize: 256, // most DEM tiles are 256 px; use 512 if yours are maxzoom: 14, // set to the max zoom your DEM tiles support // optional: give the source a name for debugging attribution: '© OpenMapTiles, © OpenStreetMap contributors' }); ``` *If you are writing a static style JSON, the same block goes under the `"sources"` object.* --- ## 3. Add a hillshade layer that uses that source ```js map.addLayer({ id: 'hillshade', type: 'hillshade', // <-- the special hillshade layer type source: 'dem', // name of the source we just added // source-layer is NOT needed for raster-dem sources paint: { // These are the default values; tweak them to get the look you want 'hillshade-illumination-direction': 315, // sun azimuth (degrees) 'hillshade-illumination-anchor': 'map', // or 'viewport' for a fixed sun 'hillshade-exaggeration': 0.5, // vertical exaggeration (0-1) 'hillshade-shadow-color': '#000000', 'hillshade-highlight-color': '#ffffff', 'hillshade-accent-color': '#777777' } }); ``` ### What the paint properties do | Property | Typical range | Effect | |----------|---------------|--------| | `hillshade-illumination-direction` | 0-360° | Sun azimuth (0 = north, 90 = east). | | `hillshade-illumination-anchor` | `"map"` or `"viewport"` | `"map"` makes the sun rotate with the map; `"viewport"` keeps the sun fixed on the screen. | | `hillshade-exaggeration` | 0-1 (or >1 for extreme) | Scales the vertical relief. | | `hillshade-shadow-color` / `hillshade-highlight-color` / `hillshade-accent-color` | any CSS color | Colors for the three shading tones (shadow, highlight, accent). | You can animate any of these (e.g., change the sun direction with a slider) by calling `map.setPaintProperty('hillshade', 'hillshade-illumination-direction', newValue)`. --- ## 4. (Optional) Add 3-D terrain **and** hillshade If you also want the map surface to be extruded in 3-D, enable the terrain source: ```js map.setTerrain({ source: 'dem', exaggeration: 1.5 }); ``` The hillshade layer will automatically shade the 3-D terrain, giving a more realistic relief effect. --- ## 5. Full minimal example (HTML + JS) ```html MapLibre Hillshade Demo
``` Open the file in a browser and you’ll see a shaded relief over the base map. Move the map around or zoom in/out – the hillshade updates automatically. --- ## 6. Common pitfalls & troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **No hillshade appears (just the base raster)** | The source type is `raster` instead of `raster-dem`. | Change `type: 'raster-dem'`. | | **Gray or flat shading** | DEM tiles are not in Terrain-RGB encoding (e.g., plain grayscale). | Convert your DEM to Terrain-RGB or use a source that already provides it. | | **CORS errors** | DEM tiles are hosted on a domain without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*`. | Serve the tiles with proper CORS headers or proxy them. | | **Hillshade looks too faint** | Default `hillshade-exaggeration` is low. | Increase `'hillshade-exaggeration'` (e.g., `0.8` or `1`). | | **Sun direction doesn’t change when you rotate the map** | `hillshade-illumination-anchor` is set to `"viewport"` (fixed). | Use `"map"` if you want the sun to rotate with the map. | | **Performance drops at high zoom** | DEM tiles are very large (e.g., 512 px) and you request many of them. | Use a lower `maxzoom` for the DEM or serve a lower-resolution tile set. | --- ## 7. Quick checklist before you ship - ✅ **Source type** = `raster-dem`. - ✅ **URL template** points to Terrain-RGB tiles and is CORS-enabled. - ✅ **Hillshade layer** is added **after** any base raster layers (so it draws on top). - ✅ **Paint properties** tuned for your visual style (exaggeration, sun direction, colors). - ✅ (Optional) **Terrain** enabled if you need 3-D extrusion. - ✅ Test on a few zoom levels and on mobile browsers (performance can differ). That’s it! With those few lines you’ll have a fully functional hillshade layer powered by a raster-DEM source in MapLibre GL JS. Happy mapping!
